newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end at year high,gains capped.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end at year high,gains capped.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures were lifted by a spurt of late buying to end at a new year high on Monday, but dealers said further gains could be limited.
After opening sharply higher on the back of the Dow's strong finish last week and a relatively stable dollar/yen, the lead Nikkei 225 June contract rose to a high of 20,835.

It finished at 20,810, 230 points above its previous close, on low volume of 7,500 lots. The last time Nikkei 225 futures ended above the 20,800 level was on December 10, when the lead contract closed at 20,845.
"The market just went up on very thin volume so it's not too convincing," a trader at a Japanese futures house said.
He said the September Nikkei was likely to face resistance near its recent high of 20,900.
"I don't think we'll see 21,000 just yet," he said. A possible correction in the Dow, following its recent streak of record closes, could put some pressure on the Nikkei, he added.
"Anywhere around 20,600 or below should be a good buying opportunity. But I would get out near 20,800," he said.
A chartist with a local brokerage also said the September Nikkei would run into a barrier above 20,900.
"We could try and test 20,900-21,000, but it will probably try and cover a gap near 20,580 before going any higher," he said.
On Taiwan futures, the June MSCI contract ended at 366.5 against its opening 360.1 on volume of 528 lots.
